# 0007. UUID v7 primary keys generated by Postgres 18

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-09-24

## Context

BUILD_PROMPT section 5 asks for sortable ids (UUID v7 or cuid2) and to document the choice. Better Auth generates its own random ids by default.

## Decision

- Every table uses `uuid` primary keys with the default `uuidv7()`, built into PostgreSQL 18 (the Neon project runs 18.6).
- Better Auth is configured with `advanced.database.generateId: false`, so users, sessions, accounts and auth tokens get the same kind of id from Postgres.
- Human-facing references are separate: order references `DLS-XXXXXX` and 12-character ticket codes, from an alphabet without 0/O and 1/I/L.

## Consequences

- Ids sort by creation time, which keeps B-tree indexes compact and lets "latest first" lists order by id.
- Ids leak the creation time; do not use them where that matters (share tokens use separate random values).
- No application-side id library is needed. Moving to a database without `uuidv7()` would need a default function or app-side generation.
